response.enhanced_information: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is primarily associated with Protein C and Protein S deficiencies. Both proteins are natural anticoagulants and are vitamin K-dependent; their rapid depletion by warfarin can lead to a hypercoagulable state and skin necrosis. Hemophilia and Antithrombin III deficiency are unlikely causes of warfarin-induced skin necrosis, as they are not directly affected by warfarin's mechanism of action on the vitamin K cycle.
